unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0012 faithfully captures the requirement that an applicant provide both names on the application when a confidential order is used.
quotes: When this occurs, the applicant must provide both her/his current and former names on the application.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0013 covers the authority to request additional identity or citizenship evidence pursuant to 22 CFR 51.23 and 51.45.
quotes: You may request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity in accordance with 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.

unit_judgments.rationale: The statement explaining that U.S. passports, Form FS-240, and Form DS-2060 are printed entirely in uppercase letters per ICAO recommendations was not extracted into any draft claim.
quotes: In accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) recommendations, U.S. passports, form FS-240, and form DS-2060 are printed in all uppercase letters.

unit_judgments.rationale: The background statement explaining that printing multi-part names in uppercase causes them to appear as one word unless separated with spaces was not extracted into a claim.
quotes: Printing a name with multiple parts in uppercase letters causes the name to appear as one word unless the parts are separated with spaces.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0014 conveys the requirement that adjudicators determine name appearance when an applicant has a multi-part name.
quotes: if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0015 fully conveys the recommendation to add a space if the previous passport contained one.
quotes: If the applicant's previous passport had a space, you should add a space on the current application;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0016 fully conveys the guidance to add a space if there is no previous passport and the citizenship evidence or ID has a space.
quotes: If the applicant does not have a previous passport and the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or ID has a space, you should add a space on the current application;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0017 covers the discretion to add or remove spaces according to the applicant's verbal or written preference.
quotes: If the applicant expresses a clear preference to add or remove space, either verbally or in writing, you may add or remove it per the applicant's preference.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claims C0018 and C0032 together cover the recommendation to space family members' last names consistently and the exception when a member prefers different spacing.
quotes: If you receive applications from several family members, you should space the last names consistently, unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0019 covers the recommendation that for special-issuance passports, family member name spacing should match sponsor name spacing.
quotes: For special-issuance passports, the spacing of an eligible family member's last name should match the spacing of the last name of the sponsor.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0028 faithfully retains the statement that name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause for rewrite unless preference was disregarded.
quotes: Name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0020 captures the requirement to change Arabic ordinal numbers to Roman numerals.
quotes: Arabic ordinal numbers must be changed to Roman numerals, for example, 2nd to II, 3rd to III:

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0029 covers the observation that some applicants may include 'Sr.' as an abbreviation for Señor.
quotes: Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0030 covers the directive to consult 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles when 'Sr.' denotes Señor.
quotes: If you determine that this is the case, follow the guidance in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0031 captures the principle that suffix issues are generally not grounds for a rewrite unless an expressed preference was disregarded.
quotes: Name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
